clue.text: Left to find out everything about burial site

indicators.note: something put out of order is disturbed, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged
about means going round, so the word for everything is wrapped round the rearranged letters

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
everything is all of it
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to learn all there is to know about a grave or tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find out' reads as discover, but out only scrambles the word before it, and everything then goes round those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A landfill is a place where rubbish is buried in the ground, so it is literally a burial site for waste.

clue.text: Vision and sound engineer

indicators.note: sound tells us to go by how the following name is spoken rather than how it is spelt

blocks.note: Gustave Eiffel was the French engineer behind the Paris tower

explanation.surface: A job advert or credits roll listing the people responsible for picture and audio on a production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound engineer' reads as one job title, but sound is the signal and engineer is Eiffel, whose name is said like EYEFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeful is a striking or attractive sight, just as a vision can be a person of great beauty.

clue.text: Charged admission for one feature of Manchester?

indicators.note: admission means letting something in, so the word for charged takes in the letter for one

blocks.note: charged as in rushed headlong
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fee is levied per person to enter some attraction in Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: Charged looks like a price but means rushed: RA(I)N. Manchester is famous in Britain for its wet weather, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchester has a reputation as one of England's wettest cities, so rain is a well-known characteristic of the place.

clue.text: After attack, crazed nurse shoved in cupboard

indicators.note: something that has been attacked is knocked about, so the letters of the next word are jumbled
shoved in tells us the nurse is pushed inside the jumbled letters

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
EN is an Enrolled Nurse

explanation.surface: A nurse, maddened after being assaulted, is bundled into a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Crazed looks like the anagram signal, but it is the fodder; the attack does the jumbling. A credenza is Italian in origin.
explanation.definitionFit: A credenza is a sideboard or low cabinet, a piece of furniture with storage doors much like a cupboard.

clue.text: Delay support

blocks.note: first meaning: a noun for a ..., a stoppage or wait
second meaning: a verb, to bear weight from below

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it sounds like postponing help; the two words are separate meanings of the same expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A holdup is a stoppage or wait, while to hold up something is to bear it from beneath.

clue.text: Unprotected attacker gets wingman

indicators.note: unprotected means stripped of its outer guard, so the first and last letters are removed

blocks.note: a raider is one who attacks

explanation.surface: An attacker left without cover finds himself a partner to watch his back.
explanation.walkthrough: RAIDER loses its outer R and R, leaving AIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wingman is a supporting companion or assistant, which is exactly the role of an aide.

clue.text: Milky Way? Yes and no

blocks.note: surface reading: our home spiral of stars in the night sky
setter's reading: astronomically it is one, but as a British chocolate bar it is a different brand from the other bar

explanation.walkthrough: Milky Way and Galaxy are both British chocolate bars, so the star system is one but the sweet is not.
explanation.definitionFit: The Milky Way is the spiral of stars containing our sun, while a rival chocolate bar carries the other name.

clue.text: Drive off around town with hack: "Where do we go for a shag?"

definitions.text: Where do we go for a shag?

indicators.note: around says the word for drive off goes round the pieces that follow

blocks.note: to allay fears is to dispel or drive them off
T is the map abbreviation for town
to hew is to hack or chop

explanation.surface: A cabbie with a fare, driving off round the town, asks where to take them for some sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Hack can be a taxi in American slang, adding to the scene; here it means chop. ALL(T HEW)AY. Shag is British slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Going all the way is the euphemism for full sexual intercourse, the destination implied by the question.

clue.text: Looks around facing this type of combat

indicators.note: around says the two looks surround the word for facing

blocks.note: an air is a look or manner, and the plural gives two of them
as in face to face, to means facing

explanation.surface: Someone glances about while confronting a particular kind of fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Two airs, one each side of TO, make the hyphenated phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Air-to-air combat is fighting between aircraft in flight, the classic dogfight of fighter pilots.

clue.text: Sick? That's vague

definitions.note: cryptic: the clue word sick is what a three-letter word means

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: sick is the definition of a short word for unwell, so it is that word defined
second meaning: lacking clear outline or limits

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a diagnosis of being sick tells them nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, sick is ILL defined: the clue word is a definition of ILL, while the whole phrase means vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ill-defined lacks clear outlines or limits, which is what vague means.

clue.text: Expected lady at first to fight for honour

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: something due is expected
opening letter of lady

explanation.surface: A gentleman is expected to defend a lady's honour by fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal one-on-one combat traditionally fought to settle a question of honour.

clue.text: Electrified track's beginning at Holyhead - bothered about length

indicators.note: beginning picks out the opening letter of each of the next two words
about means surrounding, so the word for bothered goes round the abbreviation

blocks.note: opening letter of track
opening letter of Holyhead
riled means annoyed or bothered
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: Someone frets over the length of an electrified railway line starting at the Welsh port of Holyhead.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in track's applies to both words: the beginnings of track and Holyhead, then RI(L)LED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be electrified in the figurative sense is to be intensely excited, which is being thrilled.

clue.text: Feared old fellow on entering

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the word for on goes into the word for old fellow

blocks.note: a father, the old man
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Somebody was afraid of an elderly man coming in.
explanation.walkthrough: D(RE)AD. Dread as an adjective, as in 'a dread disease', means feared.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread used as an adjective, as in the dread pirate, describes something greatly feared or held in awe.

clue.text: I see attack repelled by Italian champions

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so the run of words is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
lo is an old word for look or see
to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: A fan watches an assault being beaten back by the reigning champions of Italian football.
explanation.walkthrough: I + LO + PAN all reversed. Napoli won the Italian football league (Serie A) in 2023 and 2025.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoli is the Naples football club, recent title winners of Italy's top league and so its champions.

clue.text: Wants deposit (after home on the coast)

blocks.note: longs as in yearns or wants
H is the abbreviation for home, as in football results
a mineral deposit

explanation.surface: Someone wants to leave money with a bank once they get back home to the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed instruction sets the order of the last two pieces: the deposit comes after the home abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Longshore means found or working along the shore, as with a longshoreman on the waterfront.

clue.text: During war, a number of legit lawmen are heartlessly suffering

indicators.note: without a heart, the word loses its middle letter
suffering means in a bad way, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
are with its middle letter taken out

explanation.surface: In wartime, several honest police officers are having a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: A number is a song, not a figure. We'll Meet Again was Vera Lynn's famous Second World War song.
explanation.definitionFit: The song was sung by Vera Lynn in 1939 and became an anthem of the war years, so it is a wartime number.

clue.text: With Prime Minister at first is causing trouble

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: opening letter of Minister
taken as written
prime as in principal or chief

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister is stirring up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Prime Minister looks like one title but splits: prime means principal, and that word comes last, after the minister's initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief is playful or harmful behaviour that causes annoyance or trouble.

clue.text: Winston Smith may be another one

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could form something else when rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone muses that Winston Smith could be just another example of a type.
explanation.walkthrough: Winston Smith is the downtrodden protagonist of Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Smith is a defeated, unheroic central character, a classic example of a protagonist lacking heroic qualities.

clue.text: Discussed chances of bad behaviour in clerical meetings

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken of, so the following phrase is taken by its spoken form

blocks.note: the likelihood of wrongdoing: sin odds

explanation.surface: Church gatherings debated how likely people were to misbehave.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of clergy and church officials convened to decide church matters.

clue.text: Eye's humorous though not front cover

definitions.note: possessive used adjectivally: of the eye

indicators.note: with no front cover the word's first letter is stripped off

blocks.note: jocular means joking or humorous

explanation.surface: The satirical magazine Private Eye is funny, even if its front page is not.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is a British satirical magazine famous for its jokey covers. JOCULAR loses its J.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocular means relating to the eye, so it works as the eye's, the possessive used like an adjective.

clue.text: Jack comically takes a bit of exercise pushing back cover

indicators.note: pushing back turns the bit of exercise round so it reads the other way
takes means the comedian's name takes in the reversed exercise

blocks.note: Jack Dee is a deadpan British comedian
a sit-up is a single exercise movement

explanation.surface: A sailor does a sit-up as a joke while pushing back his blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: Comically tells us Jack is a comedian, the deadpan Jack Dee, not a sailor; cover is the definition, as in standing in.
explanation.definitionFit: To deputise is to stand in for someone, which is what covering for a colleague means.

clue.text: Old tool for two - it's in hand

indicators.note: in places the preceding words inside the word for hand

blocks.note: a paw is an informal word for a hand
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An antique tool needing two people to use it is being held.
explanation.walkthrough: P(ITS)AW. A pit saw was worked by two men, one standing above the log and one in a pit beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: The pit saw is an obsolete long saw operated by a pair of sawyers, one above and one below.

clue.text: Where animal keepers might go reportedly for film

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the phrase is taken by its spoken sound

blocks.note: a toilet at the zoo, loo being British slang for toilet

explanation.surface: Zookeepers seemingly head somewhere to watch a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Zulu is the 1964 film of the battle of Rorke's Drift starring Michael Caine.
explanation.definitionFit: Zulu is a well-known British war film, so it is an example of a film.

clue.text: Creature allegedly ingesting waste product

indicators.note: ingesting means swallowing, so the words before it hold the answer inside them

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: An animal is said to be eating something that excretion produces.
explanation.walkthrough: Allegedly looks like a sound signal, but the answer sits across creatURE Allegedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is the nitrogen compound the body excretes in urine, a classic metabolic waste product.

clue.text: Romeo in state of excitement takes both right off - the ladies love him

indicators.note: in places the letter for Romeo inside the word for a state of excitement
off means gone wrong, so those letters are rearranged

blocks.note: in the heat of the moment, a state of excitement
R in the NATO alphabet
taken as written, to be rearranged
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An excited lover removes the right-hand items, and women adore him.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo looks like the definition, a lover; it is just R in the NATO alphabet. HE(R)AT + THROB.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart-throb is a man, usually a star, whom many women find wildly attractive and swoon over.

clue.text: I agree male organ is way short

indicators.note: short means lacking, so the abbreviation for way is taken away

blocks.note: the pollen-bearing male part of a flower
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A man concedes, ruefully, that his anatomy is somewhat undersized.
explanation.walkthrough: Male organ points to the body, but it is botanical: STAMEN minus ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said at the end of a prayer to mean so be it, and colloquially expresses hearty agreement.

clue.text: See plane struggling and people

indicators.note: struggling means in difficulty, so the letters are thrown into disarray

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Watch an aircraft in difficulty, along with its passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is the first two words together; people, a plural noun, defines the nation as a group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nepalese are the people of Nepal, so the name of the nationality stands for them collectively.

clue.text: More spacious but not as safe away from hotel

indicators.note: away from means the letter for hotel is taken out of the word for less safe

blocks.note: hairier means more hazardous, so less safe
H in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A larger room is less secure when it is away from the hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Hairy is informal for dangerous, so HAIRIER is not as safe; drop the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Airier means having more air and open space, so a room described this way feels more spacious.
